Bolt actions are cheaper and suppress better than semiautomatic, and Blackout is designed to be suppressed.
.300 is a subsonic round. How far out is it going to be accurate?

You can get it in sub and supersonic varieties.

Edit: spelling
I haven't heard it being touted as a distance round like Creedmoor. Why bolt action?

Development of 300 was kind of all over the place for the first few years. First there was 300 Whisper, then 300 AAC, then SAAMI certified 300 BLK. Supersonic 300 is still not good at distance, but starts with twice as much kinetic energy and shoots a bit flatter.

The .300 BLK wasn't designed for distance, it was designed for short barrels, but it should be good to 300 yards. A longer barrel may get you a bit more velocity out of the supersonic rounds. The point of a bolt action is that you can shoot both the supersonic or subsonic rounds without having to modify or play around with your AR-15.

Supersonic rounds cycle really well with or without a suppressor out of my AR, but I try subsonics and I can't get them to work the action reliably. Even when I attach a suppressor. You have to have either two uppers- one for subs and the other for supers, or spend some coin and get a really well made upper with a good adjustable gas system, pay out the nose for factory subsonic ammunition, and also use standard loads with supers.

Why? Because higher powered supersonic rounds will over gas your system and screw up the gas impulse- basically it beats the hell out of the base of the brass to where you can see the ejector imprinted and denting the brass. This will lead to failure of the extractor, or cartridge rim- neither of them is desirable and will render your AR inoperable until it is taken care of/parts replaced.

So, the bolt action fixes this by not having a gas system, you manually operate the bolt. That way you can feed it anything you want, even your cousin's handloads using a 150gr flat nosed.30-30 (.308) bullets that would instantly choke an AR. Or load rounds singly that are too long (really long subsonic bullets can be like this sometimes) to fit into the magazine.

If this is your first AR, I would also (pretty much agrees with all the replies here) get it or build it in 5.56 Nato, then branch out into the myriad of different calibers after that first one is set up good with plenty of magazines and ammunition. That is the beauty of the AR-15, you can have it in so many calibers with just a swap of the upper receiver. All you have to do is push two captured push pins- how easy is that?
